Director Francis Lawrence had been waiting to adapt Stephen King’s dystopian novel for nearly two decades. The idea was first introduced to him by writer/producer Akiva Goldsman all the way back in 2007 while they were collaborating on I Am Legend. After waiting almost twenty years for the rights to finally become available, Lawrence faced a massive logistical challenge once production actually began.
Because the core of the story takes place entirely along one continuous stretch of road with fifty young men walking without ever stopping, traditional filming methods were practically impossible. To solve this, the production team had to design and custom-build entirely new, specialized camera equipment and moving rigs just to properly track the grueling forward momentum and capture the actors from all necessary angles as they trudged down the pavement.

The Long Walk (2025), directed by Francis Lawrence, starring Cooper Hoffman, David Jonsson, Judy Greer, Mark Hamill, Charlie Plummer. In a totalitarian United States, fifty teenage boys are forced into an annual, televised walking contest where they must maintain a strict pace without ever stopping, a grueling death march that only ends when a single walker remains alive to claim a vague, ultimate prize.
